questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose London of several reasons. First, It was my wish to study in an english-speaking country, I have always wanted to live in London and I have friends who live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I had an great experience on my semester abroad. I really enjoyed living in London with all the opportunities that are available to you, when you live there. Queen Mary and the students there are very welcoming and open, and tries to help you as much as they can. The application process for a semester abroad was easy and manageable to comply with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall I think Queen Mary was really good to send information before arrival and also to inform you about all the social events and opportunities that are available in the intro week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information about intro days, social events, and the global opportunity office held info meetings for international students in the beginning to give practical informations and answer questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult for me because I waited with renting anything before I was sure that It was actually possible for me to go (Covid) and therefore found it really late. It was difficult because housing in London is really expensive and you want to find something you can afford, and housing on Queen Mary is not an opportunity for Erasmus Studens, unfortunately. So a good advice is to book so much time in advance as you can!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing in London is really expensive and of course always be cautious of where and what you book. Also I would recommend to find a flat that you share with others both because it's cheaper and to socialise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process at Queen Mary is very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before you arrive you get an email with the deadline and the necessary steps to register. The process is different from the one the permanent students use. At the start of the semester you have two weeks to try the courses you have chosen from the beginning and within that period you can change the modules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The global opportunity team - both on email and in person when you were on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful - I got all the modules I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can always ask or write to the relevant staff if you have problems.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We got a very little selection of modules to choose from. There were eight modules you could choose and you had to choose minimum four - so that was very disappointing I think.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some lecturing was really great and insightful and the lecturers was really passionate and had a broad knowledge within their field. However, I also experienced the opposite, where the module did not really cohere and the teaching was low standard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is not that different from UCPH: Most of my teaching was lectures and seminars as we know from UCPH. In addition to the lectures there were also tutorials to catch up on the weeks subject and get the opportunity to ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public International Law

Comparative Constitutional Law 

Law in Asia

Competition Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will recommend Comparative Constitutional Law, because the teaching and the teacher is great and very professional. It is a module where you have to be very engaged and where the main part of the seminar consist of a student discussion of the main topic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had unexpected cost, but the high cost of housing was very unexpected, but something I new before I went.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and transportation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: London is a city full of life and opportunities - definitely the greatest thing about my semester abroad. There is something to do every day both at day and evening. Campus has also many societies you can become a member of and be involved in - there is almost a society for every interest. And there is Student Union, where you can register for different social events such as parties and beer night.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above there was a lot of activities available to students through the different societies - from sport to cultural activities. And there was parties and other social events every week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoy London as much as you can while you are there - there is so much great to see and experience! You should definitely consider joining a club/society on the university - it is good way to meet new people and make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have time and can afford it, there are great opportunities to visit some of the other cities around London such as Oxford or Cambridge. If you don't there is plenty in London to see - visit London's very different neighbourhoods.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The people there are really friendly and open - everyone was very interested in chatting and making new connections.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Did not find any challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Explore London as much as you can - three months is not long, so enjoy it while you are there!

Socialize - People are very interested to make new friends

It is going to be more expensive than you think, so apply for extra grants if you need it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the two-week introduction week and switch module if you don't enjoy the seminars - it is awful to be stuck with a module.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me the most rewarding part was to live in London and explore it with my new friends, but of course also to study at another university and to study in english - I really enjoyed that!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think my greatest challenge in the beginning was to get over my fear of speaking in class, but in one of my modules you had to, so that helped a lot. And to afford all the things you wanna see while you are on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
